mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate level (below 1.75%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC for FEDFUNDS predicting 20-day SPX returns is below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 4.5% signals labor market deterioration and increased recession risk, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE > 4.5, or Rank IC for UNRATE predicting 5-day returns is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate broad consumer demand contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or Rank IC for HOUST*RSAFS interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In slow industrial growth regimes (INDPRO < 105), a decline in industrial production signals imminent economic slowdown, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In slow growth regimes (INDPRO < 105), SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of INDPRO decline instances, or Rank IC for INDPRO decline signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of housing starts (HOUST) indicates robust consumer spending and economic growth, supporting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC for HOUST predicting 5-day SPX returns is below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A CPI reading above 2.5% signals accelerating inflation and potential monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 2.5, or Rank IC for CPIAUCSL predicting 60-day returns is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent decline in payroll growth (PAYEMS) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates labor market deterioration, generating negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS growth declines and UNRATE rises, or Rank IC for PAYEMS*UNRATE interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In low unemployment regimes (UNRATE < 4.0), a rise above 4.0% signals economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In low unemployment regimes (UNRATE < 4.0), SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of UNRATE > 4.0 instances, or Rank IC for UNRATE rise signal is below 0.03.
